errorCodes.meaning: No policy module with the supplied `id` exists.
The policy exists but is disabled (its `enabled` flag is false); a disabled policy cannot be activated. Enable it first via policy/upsert.
The supplied `id` is already the active policy for this (contextId, purpose). Refused so the audit log carries no no-op activation.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

activated.description: The id now active for `purpose` — equal to the request `id`.

contextId.description: Echoed from the request when it was supplied.

previousPolicyId.description: The policy id that was active for this (contextId, purpose) immediately before, deactivated by this call. `null` when no policy was active — the first activation for the slot. Recorded so an operator can roll back to the prior policy and so the audit trail links the displacement.

contextId.description: Optional trust context the activation is scoped to, for a maintainer that partitions its active-policy map per context. Omitted = the maintainer's default (single-context) scope.

id.description: The id of the policy module to make active for `purpose`.

purpose.description: The decision slot this policy becomes authoritative for. At most one policy is active per (contextId, purpose) at a time; activating this one deactivates whatever was active before. An opaque maintainer-scoped string — the framework does not enumerate its values, so each maintainer defines its own set (e.g. a community governance stage such as `join` or `removal`).
